newsitem.title: UK: Urals, West African crudes pressured by bad margin.
newsitem.headline: Urals, West African crudes pressured by bad margin.

text.p: Russian Urals got off to a weaker start of the week on Monday and some West African grades also softened, pressured by worsening refinery margins due to Brent's recent gains, traders said.

Mediterranean traders said no deals were reported on Monday as much of Europe was closed for the Pentacost holiday but at least four end May Urals and one early June were offered, with the promptish barrels bid softer than last week.

The Russian sour crude was talked around Dated Brent -$1.10/-$1.05 cif but some traders said the prompt cargoes could be bought for as low as Dated Brent -$1.20, some five cents off last week's levels.
"Buyers are reluctant to buy, because margins are very poor today. The margins are negative and unless there is a big change of trend we'll remain so," one Italian refiner said.

"The rise in Brent was too quick, too steep, and of course the products are not able to match this sharp rise," the refiner added. Brent, the North Sea benchmark crude, has gained some $2.50 a barrel since the start of May.
Trades said rumours were rife of some refiners cutting runs due to their losses. Texaco last week cut through put at its 400,000 bpd Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam.
"There's rumours of people thinking of cutting refinery runs...The alternative is to cut on spot cargoes, so the first to suffer I think will be Urals differentials," the refiner added.
A Urals buyer said it would buy at Dated Brent -$1.15 but a refiner, which said it was offered five cargoes on Monday, said Urals could be bought for Dated Brent -$1.20.
"Taking into account that third decade May cargoes are becoming quite promptish we will see softer numbers this week," the refiner said.
Despite the recent rise in Brent, Iraq has so far managed to avoid cancelling any May cargoes of Kirkuk scheduled under the $2 billion oil-for-food deal, traders said.
But attention was focused on two cargoes, the last to load in late May, one for a Spanish refiner and one for a trader.
Under the deal which went into effect in December, Iraq can export $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy urgently needed humanitarian goods.
"If they (Iraqis) get to $2 billion, the U.N. is not going to allow any further loadings," one trader said.
"There are not still a lot of cargoes to load but there's a couple this week and next week...The last one (loading), that's the one most at risk," he said.
Both cargoes are of one million barrels.

"Since the Brent prices are going up, probably the Iraqis are going to get into trouble to sell the whole quantity they have already committed but I don't know if that is going to affect more than one cargo, or even one cargo," a refiner said.
In Cairo, state-owned Egyptian General Petroleum Corp (EGPC) said on Monday it raised by 15 cents the price of its benchmark Gulf of Suez blend against Dated Brent for June to Dated Brent -$2.50.
The official said EGPC had also raised prices by 10 to 15 cents of five other crudes.
West African traders said the market was thinly talked with buyers waiting, looking at margins and awaiting the release of the Nigerian Official Selling Prices.
Traders said a few early June Qua Iboe and Forcados remain unsold and "plenty" of June barrels were on offer.
Bonny Light was assessed at about Dated Brent +45-50 cents and Forcados at a 15 cents premium to Dated Brent --- suggesting the grades have eased a little from last week.
One said Brass River was talked at Dated Brent +53 cents and Escravos in the Dated Brent +40 cents region.
There was unconfirmed talk of a June 20-21 Escravos moving late last week at a 45 cent premium to Dated Brent.

A European major said it bought a June 1-10 Pennington and late May-early June Cabinda recently but it would not confirm the respective reported prices of Dated Brent +90/95 cents and Dated Brent -97 cents.
Traders said that Asian buyers have not picked up any West African barrels recently.
One said there was talk of two VLCCs with first decade Qua Iboe headed to India and possibly one was offered in the U.S. Gulf.
--Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
